trap-negation-contrast.evidence: Pure-data table(); no trap verdict per the batch spec. Read in full. Nuclear physics CORRECT: He-4 (Z=2,N=2) and O-16 (Z=8,N=8) are the two doubly-magic entries and the only two so marked; every A value matches its nuclide. F_Pauli is not independently recomputable from the block, so the values are read as reported. Three internal problems, all reported in the notes.
trap-negation-contrast.notes:
(1) UNEXPLAINED OUTLIER: the column runs 0.812, 0.638, 0.472, 0.438, 0.368, **0.843**, 0.295, 0.296, 0.129, 0.059 - Be-9 at 0.843 is not merely off-trend, it is the LARGEST value in the table, above doubly-magic He-4, and it sits between B-8 at 0.368 and B-10 at 0.295. The parent rem:groebner-nf-computation discusses even-even vs odd-odd weight but says nothing about this. Either it is a real effect that deserves a sentence or it is a transcription error; as printed a reader cannot tell.
(2) THE 'Magic?' COLUMN IS ANTI-CORRELATED WITH ITS OWN DATA: the two doubly-magic nuclei carry the highest (He-4, 0.812) and the lowest (O-16, 0.059) F_Pauli in the table, so pairing the columns implies a relation the data refutes. If no relation is claimed, say so; if one is, it needs stating.
(3) FLOAT CONTAMINATION, and the table says so: O-16 is '$\approx 0.059$' tagged '(float)'. The parent block states the symbolic witnesses are exact Laurent polynomials only for A <= 12, so the A=16 row is outside the exact regime. Honest labelling, but per the NO-FLOAT64 discipline a float-derived value in a results table should carry the arithmetic used, and the '$\approx$' plus '(float)' is doing that work in a parenthesis rather than a provenance field.
(4) Cross-block tension: the parent says 'The $H_3(q)$ Pauli factor is $F_{Pauli} = 0.6382$' and then that 'The $A$-strand values differ because they capture the full multi-generator interaction, not the 3-strand projection' - but the He-5 row is 0.638, agreeing with the H_3 value to every digit shown. Either the agreement is a coincidence worth noting or one of the two numbers is the other.
